title: Guest command lifecycle
intro: Target contract for issue #14. The spec is docs/specs/guest-command-lifecycle.md, and the decisions are ADR-0023 to ADR-0026. These views are proposals for review, not delivery evidence.

groups.title: Lifecycle
groups.description: One owner chooses one final outcome and ends the owned group within bounds.

groups.title: Cancellation and interruption
groups.description: Explicit cancellation by exec id, separate from a disconnect and from CLI signals.

groups.title: Evidence
groups.description: The Host CLI reads a typed record and transfers one open file version.

groups.title: Seams
groups.description: Where the guarantees live and which test seam checks each one.

diagrams.title: Choose one outcome, then make it final
diagrams.caption: At a deadline or a cancellation, a non-blocking kernel wait on the leader comes first. An exited leader wins, so a finished command is never reported as timed out. A tombstone lets a cancellation overtake its own /exec.

diagrams.title: Signal the group while the leader is held
diagrams.caption: SIGTERM at T0, a grace of 2 s at most, SIGKILL before the reap, then a signal-0 probe for 2 s at most. The unreaped leader keeps the group ID from reuse. A failed probe never proves absence.

diagrams.title: Cancel on a new connection, then re-raise
diagrams.caption: A disconnect changes nothing. SIGINT or SIGTERM sends one cancellation on a new guest connection, waits 1.5 s at most and re-raises the signal. After SIGKILL, the caller runs file cancel with its own exec id.

diagrams.title: Read the record before any claim
diagrams.caption: Transport status, legacy records and invalid records stay apart. A contradictory record is EXEC_RECORD_INVALID and is never success. A guest outcome never sets ok to false.

diagrams.title: Send exactly the length of the open handle
diagrams.caption: One open, one length, bytes from the same handle. A short body and bytes past the body both fail and remove the temporary file. In-place overwrite is excluded, and fresh-name publication is the stable alternative.

diagrams.title: Place each guarantee at its seam
diagrams.caption: Candidates A and D are Host CLI work, B is the Linux agent and C is the macOS agent. Seam 1 is the process and file seam, seam 2 the HTTP fixtures with the real Host CLI, and seam 3 the disposable VMs through the app. The app relay is unchanged. Seam 3 acceptance runs only after the reviewed fixes.

discussion.title: Proposed lifecycle and evidence contract
discussion.summary: A typed exec record separates guest status from transport status and keeps the legacy fields. One owner per command arbitrates by kernel state and ends a new-session group with the leader held. Cancellation is explicit by a client-chosen exec id, and a disconnect is not a cancellation. A download sends exactly the length of one open handle, and in-place overwrite is excluded.
